text.p: Newly-merged British composite insurer Royal & Sun Alliance said on Thursday that it was on target to achieve full integration by 1998 and confirmed that it expects to see a reduction of 175 million pounds ($274.2 million) in annual costs by then.

Reporting pro-forma interim pre-tax operating profits of 450 million pounds, ahead of most analysts' expectations, the group also said in a statement that worldwide weather related losses increased by 94 million stg.
In Britain, weather losses almost doubled to 112 million pounds.
Total long term business, meanwhile, rose by 12 percent. It added merger expenses amounted to 16 million pounds and related to legal and advisers' costs.
Executive deputy chairman Roger Taylor said Royal & Sun had made rapid progress in integrating the two groups.
"We shall be in a strong position to fulfil our potential as a leading insurance company in the UK and internationally."
Group chief executive Richard Gamble said the merger would result in more widely spread profit sources, with the group less dependent on any one area of the world or any one product line.

"We now have a much stronger distribution network and enhanced market positions in UK general and life business. This will be a better base for both leveraging international growth and reducing costs," said Gamble.
However, the group did not in its statement provide any further details on how the group would achieve cost reductions.

It said when the merger was announced in May that it would cuts 5,000 jobs worldwide, with the UK accounting for around 80 percent of this. Then, at the end of July, Royal & Sun said it would close 94 branch offices with the loss of around 300 jobs.
Commenting on the group's performance, Gamble said that competition in the UK market, while still intense, had not in general "reached the levels seen on previous occasions."
"Indeed, there are initial signs of amelioration in certain classes," said Gamble. ($1=.6382 Pound)
